title: Korean culture: learning platforms and discovery resources
scope: An English-first research catalogue for people in the UK. Services, learning resources and UK participation routes are counted, not every individual course, branch, app or social account.
completeness: Broad first-pass research, not an exhaustive census. Search discoverability, language, access restrictions and changing services limit coverage.
verification: Provider pages, official institutional sources and publisher-owned UK app listings checked. Search-index evidence is used where full pages were unavailable. No paid purchase, account registration, app installation or UK playback test was performed.
cost_note: Cost labels describe the reviewed offer only. Public resources do not mean all products are free. Check plan, course and certificate conditions.
excluded_from_scope: Every individual social-media creator or lesson
Universities offering only on-campus courses in Korea
General entertainment subscriptions without a distinct Korean learning or discovery route

demand_sources.title: 2026 Overseas Hallyu Survey (2025 reference year)
demand_sources.note: 27,400 Korean-content-experienced respondents aged 15–59 across 30 countries/regions. Global sample figures are not UK population figures.

demand_sources.title: 2025 Duolingo Language Report
demand_sources.note: Korean ranks sixth among languages studied on Duolingo globally. Platform-specific evidence, not a UK market-share estimate.

entries.name: Online King Sejong Institute
entries.summary: Korean courses and cultural programmes, including food and festivals.
entries.note: Self-study and teacher-supported formats have different registration periods. The English introductory course is complimentary.

entries.name: Nuri Sejong Hakdang
entries.summary: Textbooks, audio and materials for learning Korean language and culture.
entries.note: A resource portal in the same Sejong network; some resources require an account. Kept separate from the course platform because the user task differs.

entries.name: Talk To Me In Korean
entries.summary: Structured Korean lessons, listening practice and everyday conversations.
entries.note: TTMIK Stories and its book shop are part of this entry, rather than extra platform counts.

entries.name: How to Study Korean
entries.summary: A sequenced written course from Hangeul to advanced grammar.
entries.note: A language course; wider culture is supplementary.

entries.name: KoreanClass101
entries.summary: Audio and video lessons with dedicated culture, holidays and society series.
entries.note: Check which lessons and teacher features are included in each plan.

entries.name: 90 Day Korean
entries.summary: Structured Korean courses, cultural explainers and coaching options.
entries.note: Official homepage read directly after search-tool fetch errors. Marketing promises about fluency are not treated as verified outcomes.

entries.name: GO! Billy Korean
entries.summary: Korean explanations, video lessons and supporting study books.
entries.note: A teacher-led learning site and channel, rather than a formal qualification.

entries.name: SEEMILE
entries.summary: Korean video lessons and speaking practice.
entries.note: Some learning is delivered through apps; device and regional store availability need checking.

entries.name: TEUIDA
entries.summary: Speaking practice through simulated everyday situations.
entries.note: The provider announced a Korean-for-English-speakers web version on 24 September 2026; app installation is not the only route.

entries.name: Lingory
entries.summary: Daily Korean lessons with vocabulary, listening and review exercises.
entries.note: UK Apple App Store listing checked; the separate website could not be fetched.

entries.name: LingoDeer
entries.summary: A general language app with a Korean course and grammar explanations.
entries.note: Useful for language foundations; not a dedicated Korean-culture curriculum.

entries.name: Duolingo
entries.summary: Short Korean language exercises on a general language-learning platform.
entries.note: Useful for a daily habit; do not treat app popularity as a measure of cultural understanding.

entries.name: Drops
entries.summary: Visual Korean vocabulary practice.
entries.note: A vocabulary supplement, rather than a complete culture course.

entries.name: Memrise
entries.summary: Korean words and phrases supported by video and practice activities.
entries.note: A general language platform with a Korean learning route.

entries.name: LingQ
entries.summary: Korean reading and listening with vocabulary tools.
entries.note: Most useful as a way to learn from content; not a dedicated culture syllabus.

entries.name: Korean-English Learners’ Dictionary
entries.summary: An official learner dictionary for meanings and usage.
entries.note: A reference tool from the National Institute of Korean Language.

entries.name: Coursera — Korean courses
entries.summary: University teaching on Korean philosophy and culture, plus language courses such as Yonsei’s First Step Korean.
entries.note: Check preview, full-course and certificate access separately; enrolment wording does not guarantee a free full course.

entries.name: FutureLearn — K-Culture Studies
entries.summary: Hanyang University’s introduction to Hallyu, K-pop, dramas, webtoons and digital culture.
entries.note: The reviewed course offers six weeks of limited free access; extended access and certificates are paid options.

entries.name: K-MOOC
entries.summary: University courses including Korean language and culture, leisure, and Korean thought.
entries.note: English materials and subtitles vary. A listed syllabus does not guarantee that the current enrolment window is open.

entries.name: CLASS101
entries.summary: Creator courses covering Korean language and Korean cooking.
entries.note: An English catalogue does not guarantee English narration or subtitles for every class; inspect the individual course.

entries.name: Maangchi
entries.summary: Step-by-step Korean recipes including kimchi, ingredient guidance and cooking videos.
entries.note: A useful bridge from learning a dish to finding ingredients in the UK.

entries.name: Korean Bapsang
entries.summary: Home cooking, side dishes and recipes for Korean celebrations.

entries.name: My Korean Kitchen
entries.summary: Korean recipes and food explanations, with written instructions and videos.

entries.name: Beyond Kimchee
entries.summary: Korean home cooking with photographs and step-by-step tutorials.

entries.name: Future Neighbor / FutureDish
entries.summary: Korean home recipes with video walkthroughs.
entries.note: Future Neighbor and FutureDish are one entry, not two platforms.

entries.name: Aaron and Claire
entries.summary: Practical Korean cooking tutorials and recipes.
entries.note: The wider recipe collection also includes other cuisines.

entries.name: Seonkyoung Longest — Asian at Home
entries.summary: Recipe and video instruction including Korean cooking.
entries.note: An Asian cooking resource; not every recipe is Korean.

entries.name: Hansik — Korean Food Promotion Institute
entries.summary: English articles explaining Korean food, tableware and everyday eating culture.
entries.note: Useful for understanding a meal’s context alongside recipe websites.

entries.name: Korea.net
entries.summary: Government cultural explainers and news for international readers.
entries.note: This source article is from 2022. Main/category routes returned redirect loops in this review; current navigation needs rechecking.

entries.name: Koreana
entries.summary: The Korea Foundation’s magazine on Korean arts, places and cultural life.
entries.note: English and Korean publication continues; the Foundation says other language editions have been on hiatus since 2025.

entries.name: AKS — Understanding Korea
entries.summary: Educational materials on Korean history and culture for international readers and teachers.
entries.note: Check individual publication dates for contemporary facts; historical teaching materials may remain useful.

entries.name: Google Arts & Culture — Korean Heritage
entries.summary: Museum partner stories on Korean dynasties, crafts, royal life and heritage.
entries.note: Use the online exhibits. Older references to separate Google products on the page are not evidence that those products still operate.

entries.name: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture
entries.summary: English reference entries on customs, celebrations and folk life.
entries.note: Published by the National Folk Museum of Korea.

entries.name: National Museum of Korea
entries.summary: English collection information and links to online exhibits.
entries.note: Some immersive experiences described by the museum are inside the Seoul venue; do not label every VR attraction as remotely available.

entries.name: V&A — Korea
entries.summary: Korean ceramics, textiles, fashion, design and digital art in the V&A collection.
entries.note: A collection record does not guarantee that an object is currently on display.

entries.name: British Museum — Korea
entries.summary: Korean art and history through Room 67, object highlights and a virtual tour.
entries.note: Check visiting arrangements separately from the online tour.

entries.name: LTI Korea — Digital Library
entries.summary: A discovery library for Korean literature translated into many languages.
entries.note: Catalogue visibility is not a promise that every book is freely readable. Some reading or lending services require login.

entries.name: Korean Literature Now
entries.summary: English fiction, poetry, interviews and essays from LTI Korea’s literary magazine.
entries.note: Use KLWAVE’s current magazine route; the older standalone domain could not be fetched.

entries.name: Korean Film Archive — Korean Classic Film
entries.summary: The archive’s official route to restored classic films and its YouTube channel.
entries.note: The linked guide is archival. English subtitles are available for some works; confirm playback and subtitles per film in the UK.

entries.name: The Korea Society
entries.summary: Author talks, art, food and society programmes with recordings and webcasts.
entries.note: Based in New York. Recorded material is useful from the UK; live events may follow US time zones.

entries.name: e-Gugak Academy
entries.summary: An English-facing introduction to traditional music, instruments and Korean dance.
entries.note: Course language, instrument needs and account requirements vary.

entries.name: STEEZY Studio
entries.summary: Online dance lessons with a K-pop category and video practice controls.
entries.note: A general dance platform, not a Korean culture school.

entries.name: Keens Academy
entries.summary: K-pop dance and vocal training, including programmes to follow from home.
entries.note: Formerly ED KPOP. Online training and paid travel-to-Seoul programmes are different offerings; check the selected product.

entries.name: Korean Cultural Centre UK
entries.summary: Korean language, dance, literature, exhibitions and cultural programmes in the UK.
entries.note: The 2026 language programme includes both in-person and Zoom classes. Check the format and intake for each event.

entries.name: Korean Education Centre UK
entries.summary: Live Korean language classes through Zoom, with beginner and higher levels.
entries.note: Ages 14+; under-18s need parental consent. All listed Term 2 places are closed as of this review; watch for a future intake.

entries.name: SOAS Language Centre
entries.summary: Online Korean short courses with a teacher at several levels.
entries.note: The October–December 2026 enrolment deadline has passed; do not present it as open for immediate booking.

entries.name: LingoClass
entries.summary: Korean teaching within an Asian-language school serving London and Manchester.
entries.note: Check the exact venue, course level and delivery format before booking.

entries.name: Korean British Cultural Exchange
entries.summary: A UK cultural charity with community activities and a Kimchi School initiative.
entries.note: Some prominent programme notices are from 2024–2025. They establish the activity, not a confirmed new class date.

entries.name: DGC Dance
entries.summary: London K-pop choreography classes with a provider booking calendar.
entries.note: A digital booking service for physical classes, not a remote learning platform.

entries.name: Kpopinlondonmin — KMDC
entries.summary: A London K-pop dance class and community.
entries.note: Check the class level, venue and current timetable.

entries.name: British Taekwondo — Club Finder
entries.summary: Find a local club for martial arts, sport or poomsae training.
entries.note: A route to supervised in-person learning; the directory itself does not teach taekwondo.

entries.name: HelloTalk
entries.summary: Korean conversation partners, voice rooms and community language practice.
entries.note: Peer exchange, not a verified cultural curriculum.

entries.name: Tandem
entries.summary: Find Korean speakers for mutual language exchange.
entries.note: The Seoul page lists potential partners; it does not require a physical visit to Seoul.

entries.name: italki
entries.summary: A marketplace for individual online Korean lessons.
entries.note: Choose teachers by learning goals, teaching language and availability. Official page read directly after search failures.

entries.name: Preply
entries.summary: Online Korean tutors with profile, schedule and price filters.
entries.note: Culture coverage depends on the tutor and the agreed lesson plan.

entries.name: HiNative
entries.summary: A language Q&A community for asking about wording, usage and cultural context.
entries.note: UK Apple App Store listing checked. Community answers should not be treated as official facts.

entries.name: Viki
entries.summary: Subtitled drama and entertainment for cultural exposure.
entries.note: Not a teaching course. Learn Mode was removed on 31 July 2023; UK availability is title-dependent.

entries.name: KOCOWA+
entries.summary: Korean drama, variety and music programmes.
entries.note: The provider lists Europe as a supported region. Check UK catalogue and plan before subscribing; its Viki partnership ended in November 2025.

entries.name: Weverse
entries.summary: Official artist communities and fan content.
entries.note: A fandom platform; it should not be presented as a Korean language or culture course.

entries.name: WEBTOON
entries.summary: Digital comics, including translated Korean works.
entries.note: A global comics service. Neither every work nor every creator is Korean.

entries.name: KBS WORLD — Let’s Learn Korean
entries.summary: Broadcaster learning materials for Korean expressions and everyday situations.
entries.note: A learning section within a wider broadcasting service; older lessons may use older player technology.

entries.name: Arirang Radio
entries.summary: English-language programmes discussing K-pop, Korean media and daily life.
entries.note: Useful listening and cultural commentary, rather than a structured class.

entries.name: Wishtrend — Glam
entries.summary: Beauty tutorials and Korean skincare product explainers.
entries.note: A retailer’s editorial content with a commercial perspective; not independent education or medical guidance. Link corrected on 30 September 2026.

entries.name: VISITKOREA
entries.summary: Official travel planning, cultural attractions and practical information about Korea.
entries.note: Helpful background for travellers; UK-based events and Korean travel experiences are separate categories.

entries.name: Study Korean
entries.summary: Korean language, history and culture materials for overseas Korean communities and teachers.
entries.note: A heritage-learning audience, often requiring Korean. Do not assume an English-speaking beginner or non-Korean child can use every resource.

entries.name: KF Global e-School
entries.summary: Korean studies and language lectures shared through university partnerships.
entries.note: Usually accessed through participating universities; not a public sign-up MOOC.
